questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: Which condition is true at the June solstice?
options: Every place on Earth has equal day and night and the Sun is overhead at the Equator.
The Southern Hemisphere has its longest daylight and the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn.
The Earth is nearest the Sun and both hemispheres receive equal insolation.
The Northern Hemisphere has its longest daylight and the Sun is overhead at the Tropic of Cancer.
questions.explanation: At the June solstice, the Northern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun, so the Sun is vertically overhead at the Tropic of Cancer and northern places have their longest daylight. The condition described for the Southern Hemisphere belongs to the December solstice, while equal day and night occurs at an equinox.

questions.q: The first commercial discovery of crude oil in Nigeria was made at which town?
questions.explanation: Commercial crude oil was first discovered in Nigeria at Oloibiri, in what is now Bayelsa State, in 1956. Bonny is known for its oil and gas terminal and liquefied natural gas plant rather than the first commercial discovery.

questions.q: Which vegetation belt lies immediately north of the tropical rainforest in Nigeria and is characterized by tall grasses and scattered trees?
questions.explanation: Moving north from the tropical rainforest, the first savanna belt is the Guinea savanna, which has tall grasses and scattered trees. The Sudan and Sahel savannas occur farther north, while the mangrove swamp is a coastal belt in the south.

questions.q: Which practice is most effective in reducing desertification in the northern part of Nigeria?
options: Increasing the number of grazing animals.
Deep ploughing of dry sandy soil.
Burning dry grass before the rainy season.
questions.explanation: Shelterbelts slow wind speed and trap sand, helping to protect soil and reduce desertification in dry northern areas. Overgrazing, dry-season burning, and deep ploughing expose or remove protective vegetation and increase erosion.

questions.q: Which method is most suitable for managing a forest reserve in Ogun State so that timber can be harvested without destroying the forest?
options: Allowing cattle to graze freely among the seedlings.
Annual burning to promote rapid new growth.
Clear-felling the whole forest and converting it to farmland.
Selective logging followed by replanting of harvested species.
questions.explanation: Selective logging removes only mature trees and replanting helps the forest regenerate, allowing timber harvesting to continue. Clear-felling, free grazing, and annual burning would damage regeneration and reduce forest cover.

questions.q: Which factor most strongly influenced the location of the aluminium smelting plant at Ikot Abasi?
options: Reliable supply of natural gas for power generation and access to a port.
Proximity to cotton-growing areas and textile factories.
Presence of tin deposits and a railway workshop.
Large local market for aluminium and nearby coal deposits.
questions.explanation: Aluminium smelting requires very large amounts of electricity, so proximity to natural gas for power generation is a major advantage; port access also helps with importing alumina and exporting aluminium. Coal deposits, a local aluminium market, cotton, and tin are not the main locational factors at Ikot Abasi.

questions.q: The population of a town in Nasarawa State rose from 40,000 to 46,000 over ten years. What was the percentage increase?
questions.explanation: The increase is 46,000 − 40,000 = 6,000. Percentage increase = (6,000 ÷ 40,000) × 100 = 15%. Dividing the increase by the new population instead gives about 13%, which is incorrect.

questions.q: A town grows rapidly at a point where railway goods are unloaded and transferred to lorries for distribution. This town is best described as a...
questions.explanation: A break-of-bulk point develops where goods are transferred from one mode of transport to another, creating storage, trading and service activities. A dry-point settlement is chosen to avoid flooding, and a defensive site is chosen for protection, not for transferring goods.

questions.q: A football match begins at 16:00 local solar time in a town on longitude 10°E. What is the local solar time at the same moment in a town on longitude 95°W?
questions.explanation: The longitude difference is 10° + 95° = 105°. At 15° per hour this equals 7 hours, and a place farther west has earlier local solar time, so 16:00 minus 7 hours gives 09:00.

questions.q: On 21 March, the Sun is overhead at the equator. What is the approximate altitude of the noon Sun at a town on latitude 12°N?
questions.explanation: At the equinox, noon Sun altitude is found by subtracting the latitude difference from 90°. The town is 12° from the equator, so 90° − 12° = 78°.

questions.q: Which practice is most suitable for reducing wind erosion on farmland in the dry savanna around Nguru?
options: Ploughing the soil into fine dust
Allowing cattle to graze the land continuously
Planting rows of trees as shelter belts
questions.explanation: Shelter belts slow down wind near the ground and trap moving soil particles. Removing vegetation, overgrazing and pulverising the soil leave it loose and exposed, making wind erosion worse.

questions.q: A farmer in Kwara State grows maize and yam on his farm and also keeps goats and poultry on the same holding. This farming system is best described as...
questions.explanation: Mixed farming combines crop cultivation with livestock rearing on the same farm. Plantation agriculture is large-scale cash-crop production, while pastoral nomadism involves mainly the movement of livestock in search of pasture.

questions.q: Which climatic factor most limits rain-fed crop production in the Sudano-Sahelian zone of Nigeria?
options: High humidity and dense forest cover
Short rainy season with unreliable rainfall
questions.explanation: Rain-fed crops in the Sudano-Sahelian zone depend on a short wet season, and poor or irregular rainfall often causes drought and crop failure. The area does not have year-round heavy rainfall, low evaporation or dense forest cover.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1:80,000, two water points are 6.5 cm apart. What is the straight-line ground distance between them?
questions.explanation: On a scale of 1:80,000, 1 cm represents 80,000 cm, which is 0.8 km. The ground distance is 6.5 × 0.8 = 5.2 km. The value 0.52 km would wrongly divide by 10 before converting centimetres to kilometres.

questions.q: A village is on a bearing of 225° from a town. What is the bearing of the town from the village?
questions.explanation: The back bearing differs from the forward bearing by 180°. Thus 225° + 180° = 405°, which reduces to 045°. A bearing of 225° would simply repeat the original direction instead of reversing it.

questions.q: Which instrument is used at a weather station to measure atmospheric pressure?
questions.explanation: A barometer measures atmospheric pressure. An anemometer measures wind speed, a rain gauge measures rainfall, and a wind vane shows wind direction, so none of those records pressure.

questions.q: The monthly rainfall figures for a station are 0, 5, 20, 80, 150, 220, 300, 280, 250, 120, 15 and 0 mm. What is the total annual rainfall?
questions.explanation: Adding all twelve monthly values gives 0 + 5 + 20 + 80 + 150 + 220 + 300 + 280 + 250 + 120 + 15 + 0 = 1,440 mm. The figure 1,305 mm is obtained if the last three monthly values are omitted or misadded.

questions.q: Which soil type is common on the floodplains of the Sokoto–Rima basin and is important for dry-season irrigation farming?
questions.explanation: Fadama soils are alluvial soils found on floodplains and are valued for dry-season irrigation because they retain moisture and contain relatively fertile deposits. Ferruginous soils and sandy soils are more typical of upland savanna areas, while lithosols are shallow soils over rock.

questions.q: Nigeria imports refined petroleum products despite being a major crude oil producer mainly because
options: Nigerian crude oil cannot be refined into petroleum products
existing refineries cannot meet domestic demand
Nigeria has no crude oil deposits
there is no demand for petrol and diesel in Nigeria
questions.explanation: Nigeria produces crude oil but its refining capacity is insufficient to satisfy the country's demand for refined products such as petrol and diesel. It is incorrect to say that Nigeria has no crude oil deposits or that its crude cannot be refined.

questions.q: In international trade, which document does a Nigerian exporter usually require to ensure payment after shipping goods to an overseas buyer?
questions.explanation: A letter of credit is issued by a bank and guarantees payment to the exporter when the specified shipping documents are presented. A bill of lading is mainly a transport and title document, while a certificate of origin and consular invoice serve other trade purposes.

questions.q: The stream pattern that develops on a gently sloping area of uniform rock and resembles the branches of a tree is called a
questions.explanation: A dendritic pattern forms where the rock and slope are fairly uniform, so tributaries join the main stream irregularly like tree branches. Radial patterns form around a dome, trellis patterns on folded rocks, and deranged patterns in disturbed or glaciated terrain.

questions.q: In hot desert regions, the peeling of rock in layers like an onion is mainly caused by
questions.explanation: Exfoliation is the expansion and peeling of outer rock layers due to repeated heating and cooling. Hydrolysis and carbonation are chemical weathering processes, while frost shattering requires water freezing and thawing in cracks.

questions.q: The flat, fertile land bordering the lower Niger which is covered with fine sediment when the river overflows is best described as a
questions.explanation: A flood plain is the flat land beside a river that is periodically covered by floodwater and receives fertile alluvium. A delta lies at a river mouth, a levee is a raised bank, and a watershed is the boundary between drainage basins.

questions.q: The boundary between the moist tropical maritime air mass and the dry tropical continental air mass over Nigeria is called the
questions.explanation: The Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone marks where moist air from the Atlantic meets dry air from the Sahara, and its seasonal movement controls Nigeria's wet and dry seasons. The polar front belongs to higher latitudes, while a Hadley cell is a broad circulation system.

questions.q: A community in Anambra State has bare, steep slopes where rainwater collects and deep gullies are widening. Which measure will most directly reduce further gully expansion?
options: Planting vetiver grass and building check dams across the gully channels
Paving the slopes with concrete so that rainwater runs off faster
Diverting more road runoff directly into the gully
Allowing cattle to graze freely on the slopes throughout the year
questions.explanation: Planting vetiver grass and constructing check dams slows runoff, traps sediment and stabilises the gully sides and floor. Diverting more runoff into the gully or paving the slopes increases the speed and volume of water, while unrestricted grazing removes protective vegetation.

questions.q: Crude oil escapes from a pipeline into a creek near Bomadi in Delta State. Which action should be taken first to reduce damage to the aquatic ecosystem?
options: Add detergents to make the oil dissolve quickly
Set the oil on the water on fire immediately
Contain the floating oil with booms and remove it before it spreads
Pump large quantities of water into the creek to dilute the oil
questions.explanation: Booms limit the spread of oil while skimming or absorption removes it from the water, reducing contact with fish and other organisms. Burning the oil can cause wider harm, detergents may add toxic substances, and dilution does not remove the pollution.

questions.q: A cement factory near Ewekoro emits fine dust that settles on nearby farms and homes. Which measure is most effective in reducing the dust at its source?
options: Increasing the height of the factory chimney only
Fitting bag filters to the kiln and dust-emitting points
Building a higher fence around the factory
Spraying water on nearby roads every morning only
questions.explanation: Bag filters capture dust before it is released from the kiln and other emission points, so the dust problem is reduced at source. A taller chimney mainly spreads dust farther away, a fence does not stop fine dust, and watering only nearby roads does not control kiln emissions.

questions.q: Which mineral is mined on the Jos Plateau and is used mainly in making solder and tin-plated containers?
questions.explanation: Cassiterite is the chief ore of tin, mined on the Jos Plateau, and tin is used in solder and in coating steel for tin-plated containers. Limestone is used mainly for cement, gypsum for plaster and cement, and iron ore for steel.

questions.q: The petrochemical industry at Eleme is best explained by the availability of which natural resources?
questions.explanation: Eleme, near Port Harcourt, is in Nigeria's oil and gas belt, so petroleum and natural gas provide both feedstock and fuel for petrochemical production. Limestone, coal, iron ore and agricultural produce are not the resources that attracted this industry to the area.

questions.q: In a rural area of Enugu State, many young men and women move to Lagos in search of work. What is the most likely effect on the rural area?
options: The birth rate rises immediately because of the migrants
The area becomes more urbanized and receives many job seekers
The proportion of elderly people and children rises, increasing the dependency ratio
questions.explanation: Out-migration removes many working-age adults, leaving a larger share of children and elderly people who depend on the remaining workers. The migrants leave the rural area, so the working population there does not increase rapidly and the area does not receive many job seekers.

questions.q: A town in Oyo State has a large market, a general hospital and a secondary school that serve nearby villages. This town is best regarded as...
questions.explanation: A central place provides goods and services to people from the surrounding area, which is what the market, hospital and school do for nearby villages. A satellite town depends on a larger city, a conurbation is a merged urban complex, and a dispersed settlement consists of scattered homes.

questions.q: A town is on longitude 15°W. When the local solar time at longitude 45°E is 16:00, what is the local solar time at the town?
questions.explanation: The longitude difference is 45° + 15° = 60°. Since Earth turns through 15° per hour, the time difference is 60 ÷ 15 = 4 hours. The town at 15°W is west of 45°E, so its local solar time is earlier by 4 hours: 16:00 − 4 hours = 12:00 noon.

questions.q: An aircraft leaves Abuja (GMT+1) at 09:40 and arrives in London (GMT+0) after 5 hours 30 minutes. What is the local time on arrival in London?
questions.explanation: Converting the departure time to GMT gives 08:40 GMT because Abuja is one hour ahead. Adding the flight time of 5 hours 30 minutes gives 14:10 GMT. London uses GMT+0, so its local arrival time is 14:10.

questions.q: Two places have local solar times that differ by 3 hours 20 minutes. What is the difference in longitude between them?
questions.explanation: In 1 hour Earth turns through 15°, so 3 hours 20 minutes is 3⅓ hours. Multiplying 3⅓ by 15° gives 50°. A longitude difference of 25° would give only 1 hour 40 minutes, while 55° would give 3 hours 40 minutes.

questions.q: Which of the following is a perennial crop commonly grown in southern Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Cocoa is a tree crop that survives and bears fruit for many years, so it is perennial. Maize, rice and groundnut are annual crops that are normally planted and harvested within one season.

questions.q: A farmer in Gboko, Benue State, keeps bees in hives to produce honey. This branch of agriculture is called
questions.explanation: Apiculture is the rearing of bees for honey and other bee products. Sericulture is the rearing of silkworms, horticulture is the cultivation of fruits and vegetables, and aquaculture is fish farming.

questions.q: A poultry farmer in Ibadan removes old hens that are no longer laying well from the flock. This practice is called
questions.explanation: Culling is the removal of unproductive or undesirable animals from a flock or herd. Brooding is the care of young chicks, debeaking is trimming beaks, and incubation is the hatching of eggs.

questions.q: Which of the following best explains the low level of trade among West African countries?
options: They all use the same currency and common tariff system.
They have dense interconnecting railway networks.
They have highly complementary industrial economies.
Most countries produce similar primary commodities and use different currencies.
questions.explanation: Many West African countries export similar primary products, so they have less to exchange with one another. Differences in currencies, border procedures and tariffs also discourage trade. The region does not have a single common currency or a dense interconnecting railway network, and its economies are not highly complementary.

questions.q: Hardwood timber species such as mahogany, iroko and obeche are most characteristic of which vegetation belt in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Mahogany, iroko and obeche are tall hardwood species associated with the moist tropical rainforest. Sudan and Sahel savanna are dominated by grasses and scattered trees, while mangrove swamps have salt-tolerant species adapted to tidal conditions.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1:150,000, the straight-line distance between two towns is 14 cm. If the road linking them is 1.4 times the straight-line distance, what is the road distance?
questions.explanation: The map distance gives 14 × 150,000 = 2,100,000 cm, which is 21 km. Multiplying by 1.4 gives 29.4 km. The value 21 km is the straight-line distance before the road factor is applied.

questions.q: On a map with scale 1:50,000, two points on a hillside are 6 cm apart on the map. Their spot heights are 300 m and 600 m. What is the average gradient between them?
questions.explanation: A map distance of 6 cm represents 6 × 50,000 = 300,000 cm = 3,000 m on the ground. The vertical rise is 600 − 300 = 300 m, so gradient = 300/3,000 = 1/10, or 1 in 10.

questions.q: On a 1:50,000 topographic map, the side of each grid square is 2 cm. What ground distance does one side of a grid square represent?
questions.explanation: Each centimetre represents 50,000 cm, so 2 cm represents 100,000 cm. Converting to metres and kilometres gives 1,000 m, which is 1 km.

questions.q: Which instrument is used at a weather station to record the duration of bright sunshine?
questions.explanation: The Campbell-Stokes sunshine recorder uses a glass sphere to burn a trace on a card when bright sunshine falls on it. An anemometer measures wind speed, while a rain gauge measures rainfall.

questions.q: The short dry spell that often occurs in August within the rainy season of southern Nigeria is called the
questions.explanation: The August break is a brief reduction in rainfall during the wet season in parts of southern Nigeria. The harmattan is a dry dusty wind of the dry season, not a break within the rainy season.

questions.topic: The earth and the solar system
questions.q: A solar eclipse occurs when
options: the Earth's shadow falls on the Moon while the Moon is at full phase
the Moon passes between the Earth and the Sun and casts a shadow on the Earth
the Earth passes between the Sun and the Moon and casts a shadow on the Moon
the Sun passes between the Earth and the Moon and casts a shadow on the Moon
questions.explanation: A solar eclipse happens when the Moon lies between the Earth and the Sun, so its shadow falls on parts of the Earth. The arrangement with the Earth between the Sun and Moon produces a lunar eclipse, not a solar eclipse.

questions.q: The Mandara Mountains form part of Nigeria's boundary with which country?
questions.explanation: The Mandara Mountains lie along Nigeria's eastern border, adjoining Cameroon. Nigeria's boundary with Niger is mainly to the north, while that with Benin is to the west.

questions.q: Terracing on steep slopes in the highlands of central Nigeria is mainly carried out to
options: encourage the formation of deep gullies
raise the salinity of the soil
increase the rate of evaporation from the soil
reduce soil erosion by slowing down surface runoff
questions.explanation: Terraces break the length of a slope and reduce the speed of surface runoff, allowing more water to soak into the soil and less soil to be washed away. They are not intended to increase evaporation, form gullies or raise soil salinity.

questions.q: Which of the following is a non-structural method of flood control in a riverside settlement?
options: constructing levees along the river banks
restricting building on flood-prone land and issuing early warnings
building check dams across tributary streams
dredging the river channel to increase its capacity
questions.explanation: Non-structural methods change human behaviour and exposure to floods, for example through land-use zoning and early warning systems. Levees, dredging and check dams are engineering works and are therefore structural measures.

questions.q: Removing trees from the banks of a river in a watershed is most likely to cause
options: a permanent decrease in peak river discharge
increased infiltration and reduced soil erosion
a rise in groundwater levels with less surface runoff
increased surface runoff and greater siltation of the river
questions.explanation: Tree roots bind the soil and the canopy intercepts rainfall, so clearing vegetation increases surface runoff and soil wash into the river. This raises sediment load and siltation rather than reducing peak discharge or increasing infiltration.

questions.q: The fertilizer plant at Onne in Rivers State depends mainly on which natural resource as feedstock?
questions.explanation: The Onne fertilizer complex uses natural gas to produce ammonia, which is then converted into nitrogenous fertilizer. Crude oil, limestone and coal are not the main feedstock for that plant.

questions.q: A sawmill is best located near a forest reserve mainly because timber is
options: perishable and must reach consumers within a few hours
available only in very small quantities at a time
more valuable before it is processed than after
bulky and loses weight when converted into sawn timber
questions.explanation: Logs are bulky and become lighter after being converted into sawn timber, so processing near the forest reduces transport costs. Perishability is more important for products such as milk or fresh fruit, not for timber.

questions.q: A rural district in Nasarawa State has a population of 120,000. The total land area is 1,500 km², but only 750 km² is under cultivation. What is the agricultural density of the district?
options: 1,600 persons per km² of cultivated land
80 persons per km² of cultivated land
160 persons per km² of total land area
160 persons per km² of cultivated land
questions.explanation: Agricultural density is calculated using only the cultivated land, not the total land area. Thus 120,000 ÷ 750 = 160 persons per km² of cultivated land. Using the total area of 1,500 km² gives 80 persons per km², which is the physical density.

questions.q: A population pyramid with a broad base and a narrow apex is most likely to indicate that the population has
options: equal numbers of people in every age group
a large proportion of children and a small proportion of elderly people
a small proportion of children and a large proportion of elderly people
a high proportion of people aged 15–64 years and very few children
questions.explanation: A broad base shows that many people are in the younger age groups, while a narrow apex shows that few people survive to old age. This indicates a youthful population with a large proportion of children and a small elderly group. The opposite pattern would produce a narrower base and a wider top.

questions.q: The initial growth of Port Harcourt as a major settlement was mainly due to its
options: large deposits of tin and columbite
cool climate as a hill resort
position at the confluence of the Niger and Benue
questions.explanation: Port Harcourt was founded and developed mainly as a port and railway terminus for exporting produce and coal from the interior. The tin and columbite deposits are associated with the Jos Plateau, and the Niger–Benue confluence is at Lokoja. A hill resort does not describe Port Harcourt's initial growth.

questions.q: At 17:00 on Thursday in Lagos (GMT+1), a businessman calls his partner in New York (GMT−5). What is the local time and day in New York?
questions.explanation: Lagos is on GMT+1, while New York is on GMT−5, so New York is 6 hours behind Lagos. Subtracting 6 hours from 17:00 gives 11:00 on the same day. No day change occurs because the result is still within Thursday.

questions.q: The Earth rotates through an angle of 15° in one hour. What angular distance does it rotate through in 3 hours 15 minutes?
questions.explanation: In one hour the Earth turns 15°, so 3 hours gives 45°. The extra 15 minutes is 1/4 hour, which corresponds to 15° × 1/4 = 3.75° = 3°45′. Adding this to 45° gives 48°45′.

questions.q: Lokoja lies on longitude 6°E and Yola on longitude 12°E. If both towns keep Nigerian standard time, what is the difference between their local solar times?
options: Yola is 24 minutes ahead of Lokoja in local solar time.
There is no difference because both keep Nigerian standard time.
Yola is 6 minutes ahead of Lokoja in local solar time.
Lokoja is 24 minutes ahead of Yola in local solar time.
questions.explanation: The longitude difference is 12°E − 6°E = 6°. Since 1° of longitude corresponds to 4 minutes of time, 6° corresponds to 6 × 4 = 24 minutes. Yola is farther east, so its local solar time is later; standard time does not remove this natural difference.

questions.q: A farmer in Kogi State wants to supply 45 kg of phosphorus (P₂O₅) per hectare using single superphosphate containing 18% P₂O₅. How much single superphosphate is needed per hectare?
questions.explanation: The fertilizer must contain 45 kg of P₂O₅, and single superphosphate is only 18% P₂O₅. The required fertilizer is therefore 45 ÷ 0.18 = 250 kg per hectare. Checking: 18% of 250 kg is 45 kg.

questions.q: Mrs Okafor keeps layers in Awka. She wants to know whether her poultry enterprise made a profit during the year. Which record is most useful for this purpose?
questions.explanation: Profit is found by comparing total income with total expenditure over the year. An income and expenditure account provides both figures, so it can show whether the poultry enterprise made a profit. The other records are useful for production and stock control but do not by themselves reveal profit.

questions.q: Calabar sometimes receives heavy rainfall when moist south-westerly winds are forced to rise over the Oban Hills. This type of rainfall is best described as
questions.explanation: The Oban Hills act as a barrier that forces the moist south-westerly winds to rise, cool and condense, producing orographic or relief rainfall. Convectional rainfall is caused mainly by intense surface heating rather than by a highland barrier.
